elements.problem: Angular cheilitis probable is fine. Impetigo rule wrongly requires the angle-of-mouth fissure AND crusts AND blisters, but the page says 'crusts and blisters around mouth' with no fissure requirement, and the 'and' of crust+blister is arguably too strict. Contact dermatitis rule requires fissure + severe itching; the page says only 'very itchy', which fissure is not required for. Both rules need to be independent of the fissure criterion, or at least be or-based.

rule_level_problems.problem: Requires angle-of-mouth fissure AND crust AND blister. Page says only 'crusts and blisters around mouth' for impetigo. Impetigo cannot fire from perioral crusts/blisters alone.
Triggered by any Ulcer of mouth; the page's branch is a painful ulcer with a central white patch. Over-fires.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable contact dermatitis at corners of mouth
rule_level_problems.problem: Requires fissure; page says only 'very itchy'. Under-fires.
Allergen exposure has no recency (past few hours), and 'Insect bite - wound' is a loose concept for exposure to possible allergen. Over-fires for Urgent.
Hard-requires white patches in mouth; the page only requires difficulty or pain on swallowing.

Two check_for items (Itching severe, Crust, Blister perioral) are fine, but 'Weight decreased' etc. exist only to support the diabetes rule; there is no check/diagnosis for oral candida within dry mouth or medication-induced dry mouth.

summary: The most consequential problem is the impetigo rule, which wrongly requires an angle-of-mouth fissure alongside crusts and blisters, so impetigo around the mouth will rarely fire. Aphthous ulcer over-fires on any mouth ulcer, and contact dermatitis is gated on a fissure the page does not require. The urgent box is otherwise well encoded, except for lost allergen recency.
